name: Gloria Batista
life: “I still remember carrying a valuer's bag up six flights in August.” People around Lighthouse Cove know Gloria by a small Monday habit. Gloria takes a few minutes by the low rocks, where conversation sounds different as the tide turns.
voice: I valued the view and overlooked the years she carried her shopping up without a lift. I returned with my own bags to try it.
appearance: Gloria has a long face and high cheekbones. Look for black hair twisted into a small knot. On an ordinary day, the familiar outfit is an unlined tan jacket with a pair of reading glasses in a cloth sleeve. In conversation Gloria looks down for a moment before saying something difficult.
personality: Gloria has excellent recall for voices and a poor memory for official titles. Someone who waited patiently at a counter years ago is more likely to be remembered than the person in charge.
agenda: To value the stairs as well as the view.
family: Eva Bay is Gloria’s stepsibling. Gloria puts the kettle on. Eva chooses the music. The cups come out before either brings up the reason for the visit. They trust a difficult conversation more if it has had an ordinary beginning. Asked about *An empty dedication*, Eva says, “I wrote the book while my husband cooked. He hates public thanks and likes a hot meal waiting for him.”
connections: Ruben Ali. The journalist tests the dramatic valuation against the unglamorous price of a usable bath.

reactions.situation: A relative asks for a loan against the house
reactions.response: Gloria puts the monthly cost of the suggested loan beside the home's paper value.
